analysis.title: Cross-Asset Weekly: Annual Macro & Strategy Outlook 2027/28
key_insights: Two surprises dominated 2026: the scale of the AI buildout and an energy price spike from the war with Iran. Growth surprised on the upside and central banks tightened instead of cutting.

2027 is the harder test. Growth is near its cyclical peak, AI capex adds less to growth, fiscal policy turns restrictive and central banks tighten further as output gaps turn positive and energy prices stay high.

Hyperscaler capex is forecast at about USD 1.1trn in 2027 and USD 1.2trn in 2028, from roughly USD 800bn in 2026 and USD 400bn in 2025. GDP growth depends on the change in spending, so the growth contribution fades. Hyperscaler free cash flow has turned negative and the buildout increasingly relies on debt.

Fed forecast: four more 25bp hikes over twelve months to a peak of 4.75-5.0% in Q3 2027, then cuts in 2028. The market prices only 50bp of Fed tightening against the house 100bp. ECB deposit rate to 3% in 2027, BoE to 4.25%, BoJ to 2%, SNB to 0.5%.

No recession expected. Investment is broadening beyond AI, households have de-levered, and US GDP growth eases from 2.4% in 2026 to 2.1% in 2027 and 1.9% in 2028. Euro area growth edges up to 1.5% in 2027.

AI is not yet lifting aggregate productivity. TFP has moved sideways for three years, although high-adoption US sectors show productivity gains above trend. The bank expects TFP to follow, as in the mid-1990s. Until then AI adds demand and inflation, not disinflation.

Energy: a US-Iran peace deal looks unlikely without a leadership change. Hormuz flows are back to pre-war levels, but transport risk adds an estimated USD 10-15/bbl to crude. Refined product inventories are low, about 10% of global refining capacity is offline, and crack spreads stay elevated. China's crude imports are about 20% below last year and it may have to rebuild inventories.

Five downside risks: an AI capex and equity bubble burst, oil staying above USD 100/bbl, French fiscal stress spreading to the euro area, de-anchored inflation expectations, and a wider war. Two upside risks: an end to the Middle East and Ukraine wars, and faster AI disinflation.

US outlook: AI capex is around 2% of GDP and added about 1ppt to 2026 growth. The Democratic midterm sweep should weigh on data-centre construction through regulation. The payroll breakeven rate is about 30,000 against about 100,000 historically. Headline inflation is expected to peak a bit above 4% in Q1 2027.
Fiscal drag is -0.7ppt of GDP in 2027 and -0.6ppt in 2028 (Hutchins Center). The bank expects gridlock in Washington after the midterms.

Euro area: Q3 GDP grew 0.4% qoq and 1.3% yoy. Inflation should peak around 4% in Q1 2027. The ECB is not in a rush. French spreads now exceed Italy's. The ECB could activate the TPI, and France is a borderline case. Le Pen winning the April/May 2027 presidential election is described as increasingly likely.

Switzerland: the weaker franc has brought the real exchange rate back to trend, so FX intervention is no longer needed. The SNB is expected to hike 25bp in March and June 2027 to 0.5%. Swiss GDP is forecast at 2.2% in 2026, 1.5% in 2027 and 1.9% in 2028 unadjusted.

UK: the BoE hiked in November and the bank expects one more hike to 4.25%, versus 75bp priced by the market. UK inflation is likely to average 4.2% in Q1 2027. Growth is 1.3% in 2026, 1.1% in 2027 and 1.0% in 2028. Easing is possible in 2028.

Japan: the BoJ is expected to hike in December and twice in 2027 to 2.0%. BoJ itself said it has met its inflation target but sees risks skewed to the upside. Inflation is forecast at 2.5% in 2027. Fiscal policy adds to growth in 2027 and 2028.

China: GDP forecasts upgraded to 4.6% in 2026, 4.5% in 2027 and 4.0% in 2028, supported by exports tied to the AI boom. Stimulus is expected late, once export growth fades, because of caution ahead of the 21st Party Congress in late 2027. About 100 of 376 Central Committee members are under corruption charges.

Fixed income: the rates repricing looks well advanced, term premiums are near late-1990s and early-2000s averages, and long-term real yields are the highest in decades. Long yields are expected to move sideways near term with scope for lower yields in 2027. The bank recommends 5 to 7 year maturities and carry.

Credit: spreads are historically tight but have widened off the lows. CCC and lower HY spreads have widened substantially, private credit shows stress, and spreads on high-grade AI-related issuers have widened. The bank is neutral on credit and expects more widening, not enough for a structural underweight.

FX: the dollar should stay strong on AI-driven US outperformance and Fed hikes, mainly in H1 2027. EURUSD forecast is 1.10 in Q1 and 1.12 at end-2027. The euro faces fiscal headwinds from France. EURCHF is expected towards 0.90 and USDCHF towards 0.80 by end-2027. Sterling is a cautious call, the yen recovers gradually to 155, and the renminbi appreciates gradually.

Gold: constructive despite higher US rate expectations and a stronger dollar. Central bank buying has picked up after the early-2026 price correction. Targets are USD 4,600 at end-2027 and USD 5,000 at end-2028.

Equities: a rotation that began in early October was reinforced by the Democratic midterm sweep, with tech sold in favour of rate-sensitive sectors and those that benefit from lower tariffs, oil and data-centre buildout. Equities have not recovered earlier highs despite 35% yoy Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth.

Q3 EPS growth was weak in quality. Alphabet, Amazon and Intel reported deterioration in legacy businesses, raising fears of AI cannibalisation. More than two-thirds of growth came from energy and tech. Excluding them, S&P 500 EPS growth is 11%.

Tech is downgraded to neutral. The bank prefers quality over growth and leverage, expects hyperscalers to struggle to outperform, and expects the equal-weighted S&P 500 to outperform the cap-weighted index in 2027.
S&P 500 end-2027 target is 8,500 on a 17.5x PE. Single-digit returns are expected for 2027. A fifth straight double-digit year has happened only once in 55 years (1995-1999).

Hyperscaler capex growth is set to drop to about 40% in 2027 after almost doubling in 2026. Hyperscalers issued about USD 250bn of debt in 2026 and need to double that next year. Aggregate hyperscaler FCF turned negative in Q3.

The Q3 US senior loan officer survey showed business lending conditions tightened for the first time since Q3 2024. Tighter lending standards are a leading indicator pointing to downward pressure on the ISM.

sector_views.rationale: Downgraded to neutral. Peak capex growth, rising credit spreads, negative hyperscaler FCF and legacy business erosion question the AI trade.
Tactical overweight on tight energy supply. Energy earnings growth is expected to fade with more stable oil and gas prices.
Part of the defensive and quality preference.
Part of the defensive and quality preference.
Tactical underweight per the forecast overview, reflecting the more cautious stance on the AI trade.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth was 35% yoy (blended with consensus, after 75% of reports). Ex-tech and ex-energy growth is 11%.
Alphabet, Amazon and Intel reported an unexpected deterioration in legacy businesses in Q3 2026.
The S&P 500 end-2027 target of 8,500 rests on a 17.5x PE. S&P 500 12m forward PE is back at a three-year low (20.3x trailing as shown in the market table).
Hyperscaler free cash flow turned negative in aggregate in Q3 2026. Rising depreciation on capex is expected to flatten tech earnings growth.

trade_ideas.description: Hold 5- to 7-year fixed income maturities for the best risk/return trade-off
trade_ideas.rationale: Carry should be the main driver of returns over the next few months and long yields are expected to move sideways.
trade_ideas.risk: Further Fed repricing and rising real yields.

trade_ideas.description: Favour equal-weight S&P 500 over cap-weighted S&P 500
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher leverage and cost of debt will be reflected in hyperscaler valuations and the equal-weighted index has led for most of the past 35 years.
trade_ideas.risk: A continued AI-led rally in mega-cap names.

trade_ideas.description: Long Swiss franc against the euro (EURCHF lower towards 0.90)
trade_ideas.rationale: French fiscal risk and SNB hikes support the franc.
trade_ideas.risk: The bank states FX intervention is not needed at current levels. No explicit risk named for the trade.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold, target USD 4,600 by end-2027 and USD 5,000 by end-2028
trade_ideas.rationale: Geopolitical fragmentation and central bank buying sustain demand despite higher rates and a stronger dollar.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher US rate expectations and a stronger dollar.

trade_ideas.description: Cautious on sterling, expecting weakness once the market reassesses the BoE path
trade_ideas.rationale: The BoE is expected to hike far less than the market prices.
trade_ideas.risk: Fiscal sustainability concerns flaring up would add to the downside.

risk_factors: Burst of the AI capex and equity bubble, hitting investment and consumer spending together.
Oil staying above USD 100/bbl, squeezing real incomes and forcing more central bank tightening.
French fiscal problems spilling into a euro area crisis, testing the ECB's backstops.
De-anchored inflation expectations requiring much higher policy rates and higher term premia.
A wider war spreading from the Middle East and Europe.
Rising credit spreads, tighter bank lending and private credit stress feeding back into the cycle.
China may need to rebuild crude inventories, adding upward pressure on oil prices.
Fiscal sustainability, including the Japanese fiscal stance under PM Takaichi and the UK fiscal path.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots hyperscaler capex stimulus as % of US GDP from 2022 to 2029, rising to a peak in 2027-2028 with slowing increments.
Exhibit 27 shows term premiums closer to late-1990s and early-2000s averages, with the Fed funds rate on the left axis.
Exhibit 34 shows EURCHF inversely related to the 10-year OAT-Bund spread since 2020, with R² = 0.78.
Exhibit 40 is an S&P 500 end-2027 target matrix. The 17.5x PE row gives 8,225 to 8,750 across the EPS range, with 8,575 at current.
Exhibit 46 shows five years of double-digit S&P 500 returns occurred only once since 1970 (1995-1999).
vol_and_positioning: Market-table 3M implied FX vol: USDJPY 7.6, USDCHF 6.7, EURUSD 5.8. Brent 3M realised vol 62.4, gold 22.5.
Hyperscaler debt issuance of about USD 250bn in 2026 is expected to double in 2027, adding to credit supply pressure.
Spread widening in high-grade AI-related issuers and CCC credit confirms tightening financial conditions.
Stress continues in private credit markets.
geopolitical: War between the US and Iran raised oil and gas prices, and risk of attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz adds a transport premium.
A US-Iran peace deal looks unlikely without a change in leadership in either country.
Ukraine and Russia conflict has lasted longer than expected and Russia remains an aggressive military foe.
Fading G7 economic power constrains defence spending, sanctions and policy choices.
French political crisis and a likely Le Pen win in the April/May 2027 presidential election could weigh on the EU and euro.
Spanish election on 29 November, with Italy and Poland elections due by end of 2027. German early elections are no longer unthinkable.
China's elevated trade surplus raises the risk of renewed trade tensions.
US Democrats swept the midterms and are expected to produce gridlock in Washington.

tension_points.bull_case: AI capex keeps rising to about USD 1.1trn in 2027, investment is broadening beyond AI, and productivity gains in high-adoption sectors point to TFP gains as in the mid-1990s.
tension_points.bear_case: The pace of capex growth is slowing to about 40%, hyperscaler FCF is negative and debt financing needs double, credit spreads are widening, and legacy businesses at Alphabet, Amazon and Intel are deteriorating.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp equity correction or credit tightening that hits investment and consumer spending together, or earlier-than-expected AI productivity gains turning AI disinflationary.

tension_points.bull_case: Bonds are attractive because term premiums have normalised and long yields should move sideways then lower in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed has to hike 100bp against 50bp priced, lifting US 1y/1y real rates to the highest since 2008.
tension_points.what_invalidates: De-anchored inflation expectations would require much higher policy rates and push term premia up. Faster AI disinflation would allow lower rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Banks are well capitalised, systemic stress is low and the ECB can activate the TPI.
tension_points.bear_case: French spreads exceed Italy's and a Le Pen win in April/May 2027 could lead to further spread widening and euro weakness.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A disorderly widening of French spreads that pushes contagion to other highly indebted euro area states.
